subject: biology
title: Types of Joints
welcome_lead: Bend, twist and rotate as you explore the hinges, pivots and ball-and-sockets in your body.
meta_desc: KS3 Biology adventure on hinge, ball-and-socket and pivot joints.
final_note: You now know three joint types and where to find each in your body.

concepts.def: Moves like a door — one direction.
Tough band joining bone to bone.

walkthroughs.body_html: Hinge joints in your elbows and knees move in one direction, like a door. They allow bending and straightening but not twisting.
Ball-and-socket joints in your shoulders and hips allow movement in many directions. The ball at the end of one bone fits a cup-shaped socket.
The pivot joint in your neck allows you to turn your head side to side. Cartilage cushions bones; ligaments hold them together.

mcqs.q: How does myelination increase the speed of nerve impulse conduction?
options: Myelin makes the axon thicker so the signal travels faster through more material.
Action potentials jump between nodes of Ranvier (saltatory conduction), skipping the myelinated sections.
Myelin contains additional ion channels that speed up depolarisation.
Larger animals always eat the next ones up, and there aren't enough giant animals.
